title.zh: 卷四百八十八 列傳第二百四十七 外國四 交阯 大理
title.en: Volume 488 Biographies 247: Foreign States 4 - Jiaozhi, Dali
title.raw: 卷四百八十八 列傳第二百四十七 外國四 交阯 大理 Volume 488 Biographies 247: Foreign States 4 - Jiaozhi, Dali

sentences.zh: 交趾 大理

translations.literal: Jiaozhi, Dali
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi and Dali

sentences.zh: 交趾，本漢初南越之地。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi was originally the territory of Nanyue in the early Han.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi was originally the land of Nanyue in the early Han dynasty.

sentences.zh: 漢武平南越，分其地爲儋耳、珠崖、南海、蒼梧、郁林、合浦、交趾、九真、日南，凡九郡，置交趾刺史以領之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han subdued Nanyue, divided its land into Dan'er, Zhuya, Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, and Rinan—nine commanderies in all—and established the Inspector of Jiaozhi to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Han conquered Nanyue, he divided its territory into nine commanderies: Dan'er, Zhuya, Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, and Rinan. He then appointed an inspector of Jiaozhi to govern them.

sentences.zh: 後漢置交州，晉、宋、齊、梁、陳因之，又爲交趾郡。

translations.literal: Later Han established Jiaozhou; Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen followed this arrangement, and it was again made Jiaozhi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Han dynasty, Jiaozhou was established. The Jin, Liu Song, Southern Qi, Liang, and Chen dynasties retained this arrangement, and the region was again organized as Jiaozhi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，廢郡置州；

translations.literal: When Sui conquered Chen, commanderies were abolished and prefectures established;
translations.idiomatic: After the Sui dynasty conquered Chen, commanderies were abolished and replaced with prefectures;

sentences.zh: 煬帝初，廢州置郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Yang's reign, prefectures were abolished and commanderies established.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Yang of Sui's reign, prefectures were abolished and commanderies restored.

sentences.zh: 唐武德中，改交州總管府；

translations.literal: In the Wude era of Tang, it was changed to the Jiaozhou Area Command;
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign period of the Tang dynasty, it was redesignated as the Jiaozhou Area Command;

sentences.zh: 至德中，改安南都護府。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era, it was changed to the Protectorate General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide reign period, it was reorganized as the Protectorate General to Pacify the South.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，土豪曲承美專有其地，送款於末帝，因授承美節鉞。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era of Liang, the local strongman Qu Chenmei exclusively held the territory, submitted allegiance to the Last Emperor, and was accordingly granted the imperial commission and military insignia.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenming reign period of Liang, the local magnate Qu Chenmei seized control of the region, submitted to the Last Emperor, and was granted military authority and the imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 時劉陟擅命嶺表，遣將李知順伐承美，執之，乃並有其地。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Shuang acted on his own authority in Lingbiao, sent the general Li Zhishun to attack Chenmei, captured him, and thereby possessed all the land.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Shuang acted autonomously beyond the Lingnan passes. He sent the general Li Zhishun to attack Qu Chenmei, captured him, and thereby annexed the entire region.

sentences.zh: 後有楊廷藝、紹洪皆受廣南署，繼爲交趾節度使。

translations.literal: Later Yang Tingyi and Shao Hong, both appointed by Guangnan, successively served as military governors of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Yang Tingyi and Shao Hong, both appointed by the Guangnan administration, served in succession as military governors of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 紹洪卒，州將吳昌岌遂居其位。

translations.literal: When Shao Hong died, the prefectural officer Wu Changji thereupon took his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao Hong died, the prefectural commander Wu Changji took his position.

sentences.zh: 昌岌死，其弟昌文襲。

translations.literal: When Changji died, his younger brother Changwen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Changji died, his younger brother Wu Changwen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，昌文死，其參謀吳處玶、峰州刺史矯知護、武寧州刺史楊暉、牙將杜景碩等爭立，管內一十二州大亂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, Changwen died; his adviser Wu Chubin, the prefect of Fengzhou Jiao Zhihu, the prefect of Wuningzhou Yang Hui, the ya-general Du Jingshuo, and others contended for leadership, and the twelve prefectures within the jurisdiction were in great turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiande reign period, after Wu Changwen died, his adviser Wu Chubin, Fengzhou prefect Jiao Zhihu, Wuningzhou prefect Yang Hui, and the ya-general Du Jingshuo, among others, fought over succession. The twelve prefectures within the circuit fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 部民嘯聚，起爲寇盜，攻交州。

translations.literal: The local people gathered with war cries, rose as bandits and raiders, and attacked Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribesmen rallied in disorder, took up banditry, and attacked Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，楊廷藝以牙將丁公著攝歡州刺史兼御蕃都督，部領即其子也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Tingyi had appointed the ya-general Ding Gongzhuo to act as prefect of Huanzhou and concurrently as superintendent of frontier tribes; Bulin was his son.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Tingyi had appointed the ya-general Ding Gongzhuo to serve as acting prefect of Huanzhou and concurrent superintendent of frontier tribes. Bulin was Gongzhuo's son.

sentences.zh: 公著死，部領繼之。

translations.literal: When Gongzhuo died, Bulin succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Gongzhuo died, Bulin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 至是，部領與其子璉率兵擊敗處玶等，賊黨潰散，境內安堵，交民德之，乃推部領爲交州帥，號曰大勝王，署其子璉爲節度使。

translations.literal: At this juncture, Bulin and his son Lian led troops to defeat Chubin and the others; the rebel bands scattered, peace was restored within the borders, the people of Jiaozhi were grateful, and they thereupon elevated Bulin as commander of Jiaozhou, calling him the Great Victory King, and appointed his son Lian as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, Bulin and his son Lian led troops to defeat Wu Chubin and his allies. The rebels scattered, order was restored throughout the territory, and the people of Jiaozhi were grateful. They raised Bulin to command Jiaozhou, styled him the King of Great Victory, and appointed his son Lian as military governor.

sentences.zh: 凡三年，遜璉位。

translations.literal: After three years in all, he yielded the position to Lian.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, he abdicated in favor of Lian.

sentences.zh: 璉立七年，聞嶺表平，遂遣使貢方物，上表內附。

translations.literal: Lian reigned seven years; hearing that Lingbiao had been pacified, he thereupon sent envoys bearing tribute and submitted a memorial to join the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Lian ruled for seven years. Learning that the Lingnan region had been pacified, he sent envoys bearing local products and submitted a memorial pledging allegiance to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 制以權交州節度使丁璉以檢校太師充靜海軍節度使、安南都護。

translations.literal: An imperial edict appointed the acting military governor of Jiaozhou Ding Lian, with the honorary title of Grand Preceptor, to serve as military governor of the Jinghai Army and Protector-General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial decree appointed Ding Lian, acting military governor of Jiaozhi, as honorary Grand Preceptor and confirmed him as military governor of the Jinghai Army and Protector-General to Pacify the South.

sentences.zh: 又詔以進奉使鄭琇、王紹祚並爲檢校左散騎常侍兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: An edict further appointed the tribute envoys Zheng Xiu and Wang Shaozuo as honorary Left Regular Attendant and concurrently Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The court also decreed that the tribute envoys Zheng Xiu and Wang Shaozuo be granted the honorary titles of Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，遣使貢犀、象、香藥。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao, envoys were sent offering rhinoceros horns, elephants, and aromatic medicines.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Kaibao reign period, they sent envoys bearing rhinoceros horn, elephants, and fragrant medicines as tribute.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議崇寵部領，降制曰：「率土來王，方推以恩信；

translations.literal: The court deliberated on honoring Bulin with high favor and issued an edict saying: "When all within the realm come to pay homage, one should extend trust and kindness;
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated on showering Bulin with honors and issued an imperial decree: "When all within the realm come to pay homage, the sovereign should extend them trust and kindness;

sentences.zh: 舉宗奉國，宜洽于封崇。

translations.literal: When an entire clan serves the state, they should receive fitting elevation in rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: When a whole clan loyally serves the state, they should be rewarded with appropriate enfeoffment and rank.

sentences.zh: 眷拱極之外臣，舉顯親之茂典。

translations.literal: Looking upon a subject beyond the far reaches of the throne, we shall raise the splendid rites of honoring one's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding this subject beyond the farthest reaches of the throne, We shall extend the august rites by which kin are honored and glorified.

sentences.zh: 爾部領世爲右族，克保遐方；

translations.literal: You, Bulin, for generations have been an eminent clan, and have steadfastly preserved the far frontier;
translations.idiomatic: You, Bulin, come from an illustrious clan that for generations has faithfully guarded this distant frontier;

sentences.zh: 夙慕華風，不忘內附。

translations.literal: Long have you admired civilized ways, never forgetting to join the inner realm.
translations.idiomatic: Long have you admired the civilizing influence of the Central Realm, never wavering in your desire to join the empire.

sentences.zh: 屬九州混一，五嶺廓清，靡限溟濤，樂輸琛贐。

translations.literal: Now that the Nine Provinces are unified and the Five Ridges cleared, without regard for the distant seas and billows, you gladly offer precious tributes.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Nine Provinces are united and the Five Ridges at peace, you have crossed the distant seas without hesitation, gladly offering precious tribute.

sentences.zh: 嘉乃令子，稱吾列藩。

translations.literal: We commend your worthy son, who stands among our frontier lords.
translations.idiomatic: We commend your worthy son, who ranks among the loyal frontier lords of Our realm.

sentences.zh: 特被鴻私，以旌義訓。

translations.literal: We specially bestow great favor to commend righteous teaching.
translations.idiomatic: We bestow extraordinary favor upon you, in recognition of your loyal example.

sentences.zh: 介爾眉壽，服茲寵章。

translations.literal: May you be granted long life, and wear this favor as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: May you enjoy long life, and bear this mark of imperial favor with dignity.

sentences.zh: 可授開府儀同三司、檢校太師，封交趾郡王。」

translations.literal: You are hereby appointed Acting Director of the Three Offices with the Ceremony of Highest Rank, honorary Grand Preceptor, and enfeoffed as King of Jiaozhi Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: You are hereby appointed Director of a Grand Office with the Ceremony of a Three Excellencies Rank, honorary Grand Preceptor, and enfeoffed as King of Jiaozhi Commandery."

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，璉又遣使以方物來賀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Lian again sent envoys with local products to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Lian again sent envoys bearing local products to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 部領及璉既死，璉弟璿尚幼，嗣立，稱節度行軍司馬權領軍府事。

translations.literal: After Bulin and Lian had both died, Lian's younger brother Xuan, still young, succeeded to the throne and styled himself Acting Chief Administrator of the Military Governor's Staff, holding military authority in the governor's office.
translations.idiomatic: After Bulin and Lian had both died, Lian's younger brother Xuan, still a child, succeeded to power and held the title of Acting Chief Administrator of the Military Governor's Staff, with authority over the military command.

sentences.zh: 大將黎桓擅權樹黨，漸不可制，劫遷璿於別第，舉族禁錮之，代總其衆。

translations.literal: The great general Li Huan monopolized power and built a faction, gradually becoming uncontrollable; he forcibly relocated Xuan to a separate residence, imprisoned the entire clan, and took command of their forces.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general Li Huan seized power and built a faction of supporters until he could no longer be controlled. He abducted Xuan to a separate residence, imprisoned the entire Ding clan, and assumed command of their forces.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，怒，乃議舉兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong heard of this, he was angered and deliberated on sending troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong learned of this, he was furious and deliberated dispatching an army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年秋，詔以蘭州團練使孫全興、八作使張璿、左監門衛將軍崔亮爲陸路兵馬部署，自邕州路入；

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict appointed Sun Quanxing, military training commissioner of Lanzhou; Zhang Xuan, commissioner of the Eight Works; and Cui Liang, general of the Left Directorate of the Gate Guards, as marshals of land forces, to enter by the Yongzhou route;
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year of the Taiping Xingguo reign period, an edict appointed Sun Quanxing, military training commissioner of Lanzhou; Zhang Xuan, commissioner of the Eight Works; and Cui Liang, general of the Left Directorate of the Gate Guards, as marshals of the land forces, to advance by the Yongzhou route.

sentences.zh: 寧州刺史劉澄、軍器庫副使賈湜、供奉官閣門祗候王僎爲水路兵馬部署，自廣州路入。

translations.literal: Liu Cheng, prefect of Ningzhou; Jia Shi, deputy commissioner of the Armory; and Wang Zhen, palace attendant and gate usher, were appointed marshals of water forces, to enter by the Guangzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cheng, prefect of Ningzhou; Jia Shi, deputy commissioner of the armory; and Wang Zhen, palace attendant and gate usher, were appointed marshals of the river and sea forces, to advance by the Guangzhou route.

sentences.zh: 是冬，黎桓遣牙校江巨湟齎方物來貢，仍爲丁璿上表曰：「臣族本蠻酋，辟處海裔，修職貢於宰旅，假節制于方隅。

translations.literal: That winter, Li Huan sent the ya-officer Jiang Juhuang bearing local products as tribute, and also submitted a memorial on Ding Xuan's behalf, saying: "My clan was originally chiefs among the barbarians, dwelling in seclusion by the sea, maintaining tribute duties to the imperial commissioners and borrowing military authority in this corner of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Li Huan sent the ya-officer Jiang Juhuang bearing local products as tribute and submitted a memorial on Ding Xuan's behalf, stating: "My clan were originally tribal chiefs dwelling in seclusion on the maritime frontier. We have maintained tribute duties to the imperial envoys and exercised military authority in this distant region.

sentences.zh: 臣之父兄，代承閫寄，謹保封略，罔敢怠遑。

translations.literal: My father and elder brothers, generation after generation entrusted with frontier defense, diligently guarded the borders, never daring negligence.
translations.idiomatic: My father and elder brothers, generation after generation entrusted with frontier defense, diligently guarded the borders, never daring to neglect their duties.

sentences.zh: 爰暨淪亡，將墜堂構，將吏耆耋，乃屬於臣，俾權軍旅之事，用安夷落之衆。

translations.literal: Then upon their fall and death, the edifice was about to collapse; the officers, commanders, and elders thereupon entrusted affairs to me, appointing me to manage military affairs, so as to settle the tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: When they died and the dynasty was on the verge of collapse, the officers and elders of the realm entrusted affairs to me, appointing me to take charge of military affairs in order to pacify the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 土俗獷悍，懇請愈堅，拒而弗從，慮其生變。

translations.literal: The local customs are fierce and stubborn; their earnest pleas grew ever more pressing; to refuse them would risk provoking unrest.
translations.idiomatic: The local customs are fierce and headstrong. Their pleas grew ever more urgent. To refuse them would have risked provoking rebellion.

sentences.zh: 臣已攝節度行軍司馬權領軍府事，願賜真秩，令備列藩，幹冒宸扆，伏增震越。」

translations.literal: I have already acted as Chief Administrator of the Military Governor's Staff, holding military authority; I humbly beg to be granted formal rank, to be numbered among the frontier lords—daring to intrude upon the imperial presence, I am overwhelmed with trepidation.
translations.idiomatic: I have already assumed the post of Acting Chief Administrator of the Military Governor's Staff, with authority over the command. I humbly beg that formal rank be granted me, that I may be numbered among the frontier lords. Daring to intrude upon the imperial presence, I am overwhelmed with awe and trepidation.

sentences.zh: 上察其欲緩王師，寢而不報。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived that he wished to delay the imperial army and took no action in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through his attempt to stall the imperial army and let the memorial go unanswered.

sentences.zh: 王師進討，破賊萬餘衆，斬首二千餘級。

translations.literal: The imperial army advanced to suppress the rebels, defeating more than ten thousand enemy troops and beheading more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army advanced to suppress the rebels, routing more than ten thousand enemy troops and beheading more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 六年春，又破賊于白藤江口，斬首千餘級，獲戰艦二百艘，甲胄萬計。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, they again defeated the rebels at the mouth of the Baiteng River, beheading more than a thousand, capturing two hundred warships and tens of thousands of suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year, they again routed the rebels at the mouth of the Baiteng River, beheading more than a thousand, capturing two hundred warships and tens of thousands of suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 轉運使侯仁寶率前軍先進，全興等頓兵花步七十日以候澄，仁寶累促之，不進。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner Hou Renbao led the vanguard forward; Quanxing and the others halted their troops at Huabu for seventy days waiting for Cheng; Renbao repeatedly urged them onward, but they would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Hou Renbao led the vanguard in advance. Sun Quanxing and the others halted at Huabu for seventy days waiting for Liu Cheng. Hou Renbao repeatedly urged them to move, but they refused to advance.

sentences.zh: 及澄至，並軍由水路至多羅村，不遇賊，復擅回花步。

translations.literal: When Cheng arrived, the combined forces proceeded by water to Duoluo Village, encountered no enemy, and on their own authority withdrew again to Huabu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cheng arrived, the combined forces proceeded by water to Duoluo Village. Finding no enemy, they again withdrew on their own authority to Huabu.

sentences.zh: 桓詐降以誘仁寶，遂爲所害。

translations.literal: Huan feigned surrender to lure Renbao, who was thereupon slain.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan feigned surrender to lure Hou Renbao, who was then killed.

sentences.zh: 轉運使許仲宣馳奏其事，遂班師。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner Xu Zhongxuan urgently reported the matter, and the army thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Xu Zhongxuan urgently reported what had happened, and the army was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 上遣使就劾澄、湜、僎，澄尋病死，戮湜等邕州市。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to investigate and impeach Cheng, Shi, and Zhen; Cheng soon died of illness; Shi and the others were executed in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to investigate Liu Cheng, Jia Shi, and Wang Zhen. Liu Cheng soon died of illness; Jia Shi and the others were executed in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 全興至闕，亦下吏誅，餘抵罪有差。

translations.literal: When Quanxing reached the capital, he was also handed over to the authorities and executed; the rest received punishments according to their respective offenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quanxing reached the capital, he too was handed over to the authorities and executed; the remaining officials received punishments proportionate to their offenses.

sentences.zh: 仁寶贈工部侍郎

translations.literal: Renbao was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Renbao was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 七年春，桓懼朝廷終行討滅，復以丁璿爲名，遣使貢方物，上表謝罪。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, Huan, fearing that the court would ultimately carry out extermination, again in Ding Xuan's name sent envoys with local products and submitted a memorial of repentance.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year, Li Huan, fearing that the court would eventually launch a campaign to destroy him, again sent envoys in Ding Xuan's name bearing local products and submitted a memorial of repentance.

sentences.zh: 八年，桓自稱權交州三使留後，遣使貢方物，並以璿表來上，帝賜桓詔曰：「丁氏傳襲三世，保據一方，卿既受其倚毗，爲之心膂，克徇邦人之請，無負丁氏之心。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Huan styled himself Acting Three-Commissioner Garrison Commissioner of Jiaozhou, sent envoys with local products, and also submitted Xuan's memorial; the emperor granted Huan an edict saying: "The Ding clan has passed down its line for three generations, holding a region; you have received their reliance and become their trusted support, able to follow the people's request—do not betray the Ding clan's trust.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Li Huan styled himself Acting Garrison Commissioner of the Three Jiaozhi Commissions, sent envoys bearing local products, and submitted a memorial on Ding Xuan's behalf. The emperor granted Li Huan an edict stating: "The Ding clan has held power for three generations, guarding this region. You have become their trusted pillar. In heeding the people's plea, you must not betray the Ding clan's trust.

sentences.zh: 朕且欲令璿爲統帥之名，卿居副貳之任，剸裁制置，悉系於卿。

translations.literal: We wish to let Xuan hold the title of supreme commander while you serve in the deputy role; decisive arrangements and dispositions shall all depend on you.
translations.idiomatic: We intend for Xuan to hold the title of supreme commander while you serve as his deputy. All decisive arrangements shall rest with you.

sentences.zh: 俟丁璿既冠，有所成立，卿之輔翼，令德彌光，崇獎忠勳，朕亦何吝！

translations.literal: When Ding Xuan comes of age and proves capable, your assistance in nurturing his virtue will shine all the brighter; to honor loyal merit, how would We be stingy!
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Xuan comes of age and proves himself capable, your assistance in nurturing his virtue will shine all the brighter. In rewarding loyal service, We shall be generous indeed!

sentences.zh: 若丁璿將材無取，童心如故，然其奕世紹襲，載綿星紀，一旦舍去節鉞，降同士伍，理既非便，居亦靡安。

translations.literal: If Ding Xuan proves unfit for command and remains childlike in mind, yet his family has inherited for generations over many years—to suddenly cast aside the commission and insignia and be demoted to the ranks of common soldiers would be neither reasonable nor secure in dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: If Ding Xuan proves unfit for command and remains a child in mind, yet his family has held power for generations across many years—to suddenly strip him of his military commission and reduce him to the rank of a common soldier would be neither reasonable nor secure for his position.

sentences.zh: 詔到，卿宜遣丁璿母子及其親屬盡室來歸。

translations.literal: When the edict arrives, you should send Ding Xuan, his mother, and all their kin and household to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When this edict arrives, you should send Ding Xuan, his mother, and all their kin to the capital.

sentences.zh: 俟其入朝，便當揆日降制，授卿節旄。

translations.literal: Once they enter court, We shall promptly issue an edict on a chosen day appointing you with the military insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Once they arrive at court, We shall promptly issue a decree appointing you with full military insignia.

sentences.zh: 凡茲兩途，卿宜審處其一。

translations.literal: Of these two courses, you should carefully choose one.
translations.idiomatic: Between these two courses of action, you should carefully choose one.

sentences.zh: 丁璿到京，必加優禮。

translations.literal: When Ding Xuan reaches the capital, he shall certainly receive exceptional honors.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Xuan reaches the capital, he shall certainly receive exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 今遣供奉官張宗權齎詔諭旨，當悉朕懷。」

translations.literal: We now send the palace attendant Zhang Zongquan bearing this edict to convey Our intent—you should fully understand Our mind.
translations.idiomatic: We now dispatch the palace attendant Zhang Zongquan to deliver this edict and convey Our intent. You should understand Our full meaning.

sentences.zh: 亦賜璿詔書如旨。

translations.literal: An edict was also granted to Xuan to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the same purport was also granted to Ding Xuan.

sentences.zh: 時黎桓已專據其土，不聽命。

translations.literal: By this time Li Huan had already exclusively occupied the territory and would not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Li Huan had seized exclusive control of the region and refused to obey imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 是歲五月上言，占城國水陸象馬數萬來寇，率所部兵擊走之，俘斬千計。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he submitted a report that Champa had sent tens of thousands of troops by land and sea with elephants to raid; he led his forces to repulse them, capturing and slaying on the order of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year, he reported that Champa had launched a raid with tens of thousands of troops and war elephants by land and sea. He led his forces to repulse them, capturing and slaying roughly a thousand.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，遣牙校張紹馮、阮伯簪等貢方物，繼上表求正領節鎮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, he sent the ya-officers Zhang Shaofeng, Ruan Bozan, and others with local products as tribute, followed by a memorial requesting formal appointment as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongxi reign period, he sent the ya-officers Zhang Shaofeng, Ruan Bozan, and others bearing local products as tribute, followed by a memorial requesting formal appointment as military governor.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，又遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, envoys were again sent with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year, he again sent envoys bearing local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 儋州言，占城國人蒲羅遏率其族百餘衆內附，言爲交州所逼故也。

translations.literal: Danzhou reported that the Champa native Pu Luoe led more than a hundred of his clan to submit to the empire, saying they had been forced by Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhou reported that the Champa native Pu Luoe had led more than a hundred members of his clan to submit to the Song, stating that they had been driven out by Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，制曰：「王者懋建皇極，寵綏列藩。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, an edict stated: "The sovereign diligently establishes the supreme principle, favoring and comforting the frontier lords.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year, an imperial decree stated: "The sovereign diligently upholds the supreme principle of governance, favoring and reassuring the frontier lords.

sentences.zh: 設邸京師，所以盛會同之禮；

translations.literal: Establishing lodges in the capital is to magnify the rites of gathering in harmony;
translations.idiomatic: Establishing lodges in the capital serves to honor the rites of gathering in harmony at court;

sentences.zh: 胙土方面，所以表節制之雄。

translations.literal: Enfeoffing land in the regions is to display the majesty of military governance.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffing territory in the frontier regions displays the sovereign authority of military command.

sentences.zh: 矧茲ㄢ鳶之隅，克修設羽之貢，式當易帥，爰利建侯，不忘請命之恭，用舉醻勞之典。

translations.literal: Moreover, in this remote corner beyond the wild geese, having dutifully maintained tribute of feathered offerings—now rightly time to change commanders, thereby beneficial to enfeoff lords, not forgetting the deference of petitioning for appointment, we hereby perform the rite of rewarding labor.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in this remote corner beyond the wild geese' flight, where tribute has been faithfully maintained—the time has come to change commanders and enfeoff a worthy lord. In recognition of the loyalty shown in petitioning for appointment, We hereby perform the rite of rewarding distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 權知交州三使留後黎桓，兼資義勇，特稟忠純，能得邦人之心，彌謹藩臣之禮。

translations.literal: The Acting Three-Commissioner Garrison Commissioner of Jiaozhou Li Huan, possessing both righteousness and courage, especially endowed with loyalty and integrity, able to win the hearts of his people, ever more diligent in the rites due a frontier subject—
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, Acting Garrison Commissioner of the Three Jiaozhi Commissions, possesses both courage and righteousness and is endowed with exceptional loyalty and integrity. He has won the hearts of his people and is ever diligent in the duties owed a frontier subject.

sentences.zh: 往者，丁璿方在童幼，昧於撫綏。

translations.literal: Previously, when Ding Xuan was still in childhood, he was ignorant of governance and soothing.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Ding Xuan was still a child, he was incapable of governing and pacifying the realm.

sentences.zh: 桓乃肺腑之親，專掌軍旅之事，號令自出，威愛並行。

translations.literal: Huan, a close kinsman by marriage, exclusively controlled military affairs; orders issued from himself alone; authority and benevolence were exercised together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, a close kinsman by marriage, took exclusive charge of military affairs. Orders issued from his hand alone, and he exercised both authority and benevolence in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 璿盡解三使之權，以徇衆人之欲。

translations.literal: Xuan fully relinquished the authority of the three commissioners to comply with the people's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xuan fully relinquished the authority of the three commissions to satisfy the wishes of the people.

sentences.zh: 遠輸誠款，求領節旄。

translations.literal: From afar he has conveyed sincere allegiance, seeking to hold the military insignia.
translations.idiomatic: From afar he has conveyed his sincere allegiance, seeking formal appointment with full military insignia.

sentences.zh: 土燮強明，化越俗而鹹乂；

translations.literal: Tu Shi was strong and enlightened, transforming Yue customs until all was well ordered;
translations.idiomatic: Tu Shi was strong and enlightened, transforming the customs of Yue until the land was well governed;

sentences.zh: 尉佗恭順，稟漢詔以無違。

translations.literal: Zhao Tuo was respectful and obedient, receiving Han edicts without violation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tuo was respectful and obedient, receiving Han imperial edicts without violation.

sentences.zh: 宜正元戎之稱，以列通侯之貴，控撫夷落，對揚天休。

translations.literal: He should be granted the title of supreme commander, ranked with the nobility of full marquis, to control and soothe the tribal settlements, giving voice to Heaven's blessings.
translations.idiomatic: He should be granted the title of supreme commander and ranked among the most honored marquises, to govern and pacify the tribal peoples and give voice to Heaven's blessings upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 可檢校太保、使持節、都督交州諸軍事、安南都護，充靜海軍節度、交州管內觀察處置等使，封京兆郡侯，食邑三千戶，仍賜號推誠順化功臣。」

translations.literal: He is appointed honorary Grand Guardian, commissioned with the staff of authority, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Jiaozhou, Protector-General of Annan, Military Governor of the Jinghai Army and Commissioner for Observation and Disposition within Jiaozhou Circuit, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingzhao Commandery with a fief of three thousand households, and additionally granted the title Merit Subject of Sincere Submission and Harmonious Transformation."
translations.idiomatic: He is hereby appointed honorary Grand Guardian, commissioned with the staff of authority as Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Jiaozhi, Protector-General to Pacify the South, Military Governor of the Jinghai Army and Commissioner for Observation and Disposition within Jiaozhi Circuit, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingzhao Commandery with a fief of three thousand households, and granted the honorific title Merit Subject of Sincere Submission and Harmonious Transformation."

sentences.zh: 遣左補闕李若拙、國子博士李覺爲使以賜之。

translations.literal: The Left Supplementation Censor Li Ruozhuo and the Erudite of the Imperial Academy Li Jue were dispatched as envoys to confer it upon him.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Supplementation Censor Li Ruozhuo and Imperial Academy Erudite Li Jue were dispatched as envoys to deliver the appointment.

sentences.zh: 去歲秋末抵交州境，桓遣牙內都指揮使丁承正等以船九艘、卒三百人至太平軍來迎，由海口入大海，冒涉風濤，頗曆危險。

translations.literal: At the end of autumn last year they reached the border of Jiaozhou; Huan sent the ya-inner commander Ding Chengzheng and others with nine ships and three hundred soldiers to Taiping Army to welcome them; entering the sea from the river mouth, they braved wind and waves and experienced considerable danger.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the previous autumn, they reached the border of Jiaozhi. Li Huan sent the commander of the inner guard Ding Chengzheng and others with nine ships and three hundred soldiers to Taiping Army to welcome them. Entering the sea from the river mouth, they braved wind and waves and faced considerable peril.

sentences.zh: 經半月至白藤，徑入海氵義，乘潮而行。

translations.literal: After half a month they reached Baiteng, directly entering the coastal channel, traveling with the tide.
translations.idiomatic: After half a month they reached Baiteng and entered the coastal channel directly, traveling with the tide.

sentences.zh: 凡宿泊之所皆有茅舍三間，營葺尚新，目爲館驛。

translations.literal: At every anchorage there were three thatched huts, newly maintained, regarded as relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: At every anchorage there were three thatched huts, freshly maintained and serving as relay stations.

sentences.zh: 至長州漸近本國，桓張惶虛誕，務爲誇詫，盡出舟師戰棹，謂之耀軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Changzhou they gradually neared the native state; Huan, in alarm and extravagance, striving to boast, deployed all his naval warships, calling it a display of military might.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Changzhou they drew near Li Huan's realm. Li Huan, agitated and prone to exaggeration, strove to impress them by deploying his entire fleet of warships in what he called a display of military might.

sentences.zh: 自是宵征抵海岸，至交州僅十五里，有茅亭五間，題曰茅徑驛。

translations.literal: From there they traveled by night to reach the coast; fifteen li from Jiaozhou there were five thatched pavilions, inscribed "Maojing Relay Station."
translations.idiomatic: From there they traveled by night until they reached the coast. Fifteen li from Jiaozhou stood five thatched pavilions bearing the inscription "Maojing Relay Station."

sentences.zh: 至城一百里，驅部民畜產，妄稱官牛，數不滿千，揚言十萬。

translations.literal: A hundred li from the city, he drove the local people's livestock, falsely calling them government cattle; the number was less than a thousand, yet he proclaimed one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li from the city, he drove out the local people's livestock and falsely claimed them as government cattle. Though fewer than a thousand in number, he proclaimed that there were one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 又廣率其民混於軍旅，衣以雜色之衣，乘船鼓噪。

translations.literal: He also broadly conscripted the people to mingle with the army troops, clothed in motley garments, boarding boats and raising clamor.
translations.idiomatic: He also marshaled large numbers of civilians to mingle with his troops, dressed them in motley clothing, and had them board boats to raise a clamor.

sentences.zh: 近城之山虛張白旗，以爲陳兵之象。

translations.literal: On the mountains near the city, white banners were falsely displayed to create the appearance of deployed troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the hills near the city, white banners were falsely displayed to create the impression of massed troops.

sentences.zh: 俄而擁從桓至，展郊迎之禮，桓斂馬側身，問皇帝起居畢，按轡偕行。

translations.literal: Before long, Huan arrived with an escort, performed the rite of welcoming guests outside the suburbs; Huan reined in his horse and turned aside, inquired after the emperor's health, then pressed the reins and walked together.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Huan arrived with an escort and performed the suburban welcome rites. He reined in his horse and turned respectfully aside, inquired after the emperor's health, and then rode side by side with the envoys.

sentences.zh: 時以檳榔相遺，馬上食之，此風俗待賓之厚意也。

translations.literal: At the time betel nuts were exchanged as gifts; they were eaten on horseback—this was the local custom of generously treating guests.
translations.idiomatic: Betel nuts were exchanged as gifts and eaten on horseback—this was the local custom of generously honoring guests.

sentences.zh: 城中無居民，止有茅竹屋數十百區，以爲軍營。

translations.literal: Within the city there were no residents, only several dozen or hundred sections of thatched bamboo dwellings serving as military camps.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city there were no civilian residents—only several dozen to a hundred thatched bamboo structures serving as military camps.

sentences.zh: 而府署湫隘，題其門曰明德門。

translations.literal: The government offices were cramped and narrow; its gate was inscribed "Gate of Bright Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The government offices were cramped and mean, and their gate bore the inscription "Gate of Bright Virtue."

sentences.zh: 桓質陋而目眇，自言近歲與蠻寇接戰，墜馬傷足，受詔不拜。

translations.literal: Huan was plain in appearance and blind in one eye; he said that in recent years, fighting border raiders, he had fallen from his horse and injured his foot, and therefore did not kneel when receiving the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was plain in appearance and blind in one eye. He claimed that in recent years, while fighting tribal raiders, he had fallen from his horse and injured his foot, and on these grounds did not kneel when receiving the imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 信宿之後，乃張筵飲宴。

translations.literal: After two nights' lodging, he then spread a banquet for feasting.
translations.idiomatic: After two nights' stay, he hosted a banquet in their honor.

sentences.zh: 又出臨海氵義，以爲娛賓之遊。

translations.literal: He again went out to the coastal channel as an excursion to entertain the guests.
translations.idiomatic: He then took them out to the coastal channel as an excursion to entertain the guests.

sentences.zh: 桓跣足持竿，入水標魚，每中一魚，左右皆叫噪歡躍。

translations.literal: Huan, barefoot, held a rod, entered the water to spear fish; each time he struck a fish, those around him all shouted and leaped in joy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan went barefoot with a spear in hand, waded into the water to fish. Each time he speared a fish, those around him shouted and leaped for joy.

sentences.zh: 凡有宴會，預坐之人悉令解帶，冠以帽子。

translations.literal: Whenever there were banquets, all those seated in advance were ordered to loosen their belts and put on caps.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet, all guests seated beforehand were ordered to loosen their belts and wear caps.

sentences.zh: 桓多衣花纈及紅色之衣，帽以真珠爲飾，或自歌勸酒，莫能曉其詞。

translations.literal: Huan often wore patterned tie-dye and red clothing; his cap was adorned with pearls; sometimes he sang himself to urge drinking, and none could understand his words.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan often wore tie-dyed patterns and red garments, his cap studded with pearls. Sometimes he sang to urge the guests to drink, but no one could make out his words.

sentences.zh: 嘗令數十人扛大蛇長數丈，饋於使館，且曰：「若能食此，當治之爲饌以獻焉。」

translations.literal: Once he had several dozen men carry a great snake several zhang long and present it to the envoy quarters, saying: "If you can eat this, I shall have it prepared as a dish and presented."
translations.idiomatic: Once he had several dozen men carry a great snake several zhang in length and present it at the envoys' quarters, saying, "If you can eat this, I will have it cooked as a dish and served to you.

sentences.zh: 又羈送二虎，以備縱觀。

translations.literal: He also sent two caged tigers for release and viewing.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent two caged tigers, intended for release and viewing.

sentences.zh: 皆卻之不受。

translations.literal: All were declined and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys declined everything and accepted none of it.

sentences.zh: 士卒殆三千人，悉黥其額曰「天子軍」。

translations.literal: The soldiers numbered nearly three thousand; all had their foreheads tattooed with the words "Imperial Army."
translations.idiomatic: The troops numbered nearly three thousand; every man's forehead was tattooed with the words "Imperial Army."

sentences.zh: 糧以禾穗日給，令自舂爲食。

translations.literal: Grain was supplied daily as ears of millet on the stalk, and they were ordered to husk it themselves for food.
translations.idiomatic: Rations were issued daily as millet still on the stalk, and the men were made to husk and grind it themselves for their meals.

sentences.zh: 兵器止有弓弩、木牌、梭槍、竹槍，弱不可用。

translations.literal: Their weapons consisted only of bows and crossbows, wooden shields, shuttle spears, and bamboo spears—weak and unserviceable.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms amounted only to bows and crossbows, wooden shields, shuttle spears, and bamboo spears—feeble and barely usable.

sentences.zh: 桓輕亻兌殘忍，昵比小人，腹心閹豎五七輩錯立其側。

translations.literal: Huan was frivolous, overbearing, and cruel; he kept company with petty men, and five or six trusted eunuchs stood mixed about at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was frivolous, overbearing, and cruel. He consorted with petty men, and five or six trusted eunuchs stood always at his side.

sentences.zh: 好狎飲，以手令爲樂。

translations.literal: He loved convivial drinking and took hand-signal games as his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He loved boisterous drinking and amused himself with hand-signal drinking games.

sentences.zh: 凡官屬善其事者，擢居親近左右，有小過亦殺之，或鞭其背一百至二百。

translations.literal: Those among his subordinates who were skilled at such things were promoted to positions close at his side; even for minor faults he would kill them, or whip their backs one hundred to two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who excelled at such diversions were promoted to positions close at hand. Even for minor offenses he would put them to death, or lash their backs one hundred to two hundred times.

sentences.zh: 賓佐小不如意，亦捶之三十至五十，黜爲閽吏；

translations.literal: If aides were slightly displeasing, he also beat them thirty to fifty strokes and demoted them to gate attendants;
translations.idiomatic: If an aide displeased him even slightly, he would beat him thirty to fifty strokes and demote him to gate attendant;

sentences.zh: 怒息，乃召復其位。

translations.literal: When his anger subsided, he would summon them back and restore their positions.
translations.idiomatic: when his anger passed, he would summon them back and restore their former posts.

sentences.zh: 有木塔，其制樸陋，桓一日請同登遊覽。

translations.literal: There was a wooden pagoda, plain and crude in construction; one day Huan invited them to climb it together for a view.
translations.idiomatic: There was a wooden pagoda, plain and crude in build. One day Li Huan invited the envoys to climb it with him for the view.

sentences.zh: 地無寒氣，十一月猶衣夾衣揮扇云。

translations.literal: The land had no cold air; even in the eleventh month one still wore unlined jackets and waved fans, they said.
translations.idiomatic: The region knew no cold; even in the eleventh month people still wore light jackets and fanned themselves, they said.

sentences.zh: 先是，欽州如洪、咄步、如昔等三鎮皆瀕海，交州潮陽民卜文勇等殺人，並家亡命至如昔鎮，鎮將黃令德等匿之。

translations.literal: Previously, the three stockades of Ruhong, Duobu, and Ruxi in Qin Prefecture all bordered the sea. The Chaoyang townsman Bu Wenyong of Jiaozhi and others committed murder and fled with their families to Ruxi Stockade; the stockade commander Huang Lingde and others hid them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the three coastal stockades of Ruhong, Duobu, and Ruxi in Qin Prefecture all lay on the sea. Bu Wenyong of Chaoyang in Jiaozhi and others committed murder and fled with their families to Ruxi Stockade, where the commander Huang Lingde and his men sheltered them.

sentences.zh: 桓令潮陽鎮將黃成雅移牒來捕，令德固不遣，因茲海賊連年剽掠。

translations.literal: Huan ordered the Chaoyang stockade commander Huang Chengya to send a dispatch to arrest them, but Lingde firmly refused to surrender them; because of this, sea bandits raided and plundered year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan ordered the Chaoyang stockade commander Huang Chengya to send a dispatch demanding their surrender, but Lingde refused to hand them over. Sea bandits therefore raided and plundered year after year.

sentences.zh: 二年，以工部員外郎、直史館陳堯叟爲轉運使，因賜桓詔書。

translations.literal: In the second year, Chen Yaosou, Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and Compiler at the Historical Archives, was appointed transport commissioner, and an imperial edict was granted to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Chen Yaosou, Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and Compiler at the Historical Archives, was appointed transport commissioner for the circuit, and an imperial edict was sent to Li Huan.

sentences.zh: 堯叟始至，遣攝雷州海康縣尉李建中齎詔勞問桓。

translations.literal: When Yaosou first arrived, he sent Acting Haikang County Lieutenant Li Jianzhong of Leizhou to carry the edict and convey imperial regards to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaosou first arrived, he dispatched Li Jianzhong, acting county lieutenant of Haikang in Leizhou, to carry the edict and convey the court's regards to Li Huan.

sentences.zh: 堯叟又至如昔，詰得匿文勇之由，盡擒其男女老少一百三十口，召潮陽鎮吏付之，且戒勿加酷法。

translations.literal: Yaosou then went to Ruxi, interrogated and learned the reason Wenyong had been hidden, seized all the men, women, and children—one hundred thirty persons in all—summoned Chaoyang stockade officials and handed them over, and enjoined them not to apply cruel punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yaosou then went to Ruxi, investigated how Wenyong had been concealed, and seized all one hundred thirty men, women, and children involved. He summoned officials of Chaoyang Stockade, handed the prisoners over to them, and strictly forbade cruel punishment.

sentences.zh: 成雅得其人，以狀謝堯叟。

translations.literal: Chengya received the prisoners and sent a report thanking Yaosou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengya received the prisoners and submitted a report of thanks to Yaosou.

sentences.zh: 桓遂上章感恩，並捕海賊二十五人送於堯叟，且言已約勒溪洞首領，不得騷動。

translations.literal: Huan then submitted a memorial expressing gratitude, also captured twenty-five sea bandits and sent them to Yaosou, and stated that he had already restrained the chieftains of stream grottoes and ravines from causing disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan then submitted a memorial of gratitude, captured twenty-five sea bandits and sent them to Yaosou, and reported that he had already bound the chieftains of the stream grottoes not to cause unrest.

sentences.zh: 七月，太宗遣主客郎中、直昭文館李若拙齎詔書，充國信使，以美玉帶往賜桓。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Emperor Taizong dispatched Bureau Director of the Host Directorate and Compiler at the Hall of Splendid Literature Li Ruozhuo, bearing an imperial edict, to serve as credentialed envoy and bring a fine jade belt to bestow upon Huan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Emperor Taizong dispatched Li Ruozhuo, Bureau Director of the Host Directorate and Compiler at the Hall of Splendid Literature, bearing an imperial edict as credentialed envoy, to bring a fine jade belt and bestow it upon Li Huan.

sentences.zh: 若拙既至，桓出郊迎，然其詞氣尚悖慢，謂若拙曰：「向者劫如洪鎮乃外境蠻賊也，皇帝知此非交州兵否？

translations.literal: When Ruozhuo arrived, Huan went out to the suburbs to welcome him, yet his tone remained defiant and insolent; he said to Ruozhuo: "The earlier raid on Ruhong Stockade was carried out by foreign-border barbarian bandits—does the Emperor know that these were not Jiaozhi troops?
translations.idiomatic: When Ruozhuo arrived, Li Huan went out to the suburbs to welcome him, yet his words remained defiant and insolent. He said to Ruozhuo, "The earlier attack on Ruhong Stockade was the work of barbarian bandits from beyond the border. Does the Emperor know they were not troops of Jiaozhi?

sentences.zh: 若使交州果叛命，則當首攻番禺，次擊閩、越，豈止如洪鎮而已！」

translations.literal: If Jiaozhi truly rebelled, then we should first attack Panyu, then strike Min and Yue—how could it be limited to Ruhong Stockade alone!"
translations.idiomatic: If Jiaozhi truly rebelled, we would first strike Panyu, then hit Min and Yue—how could it stop at Ruhong Stockade alone!"

sentences.zh: 若拙從容謂桓曰：「上初聞寇如洪鎮，雖未知其所自，然以足下拔自交州牙校，授之節制，固當盡忠以報，豈有他慮！

translations.literal: Ruozhuo calmly said to Huan: "When His Majesty first heard of the attack on Ruhong Stockade, though he did not yet know its source, since you were raised from a ya-general of Jiaozhi and granted military commission, you surely ought to repay that with full loyalty—how could there be any other concern!
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhuo calmly replied to Li Huan, "When His Majesty first heard of the raid on Ruhong Stockade, he did not yet know who was responsible. But you were raised from a ya-general in Jiaozhi and invested with command—surely you ought to repay that with full loyalty. What other concern could there be?

sentences.zh: 及見執送海賊，事果明白。

translations.literal: Once he saw the captured sea bandits sent forward, the matter indeed became clear.
translations.idiomatic: Once the captured sea bandits were delivered, the matter became perfectly clear.

sentences.zh: 然而大臣僉議，以爲朝廷比建節帥，以寧海表，今既蠻賊爲寇害，乃是交州力不能獨制矣。

translations.literal: However, the high ministers all deliberated together, holding that the court had recently established a military commissioner to pacify the maritime frontier; now that barbarian bandits were causing harm, Jiaozhi's strength alone could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the high ministers jointly concluded that the court had lately established a military commissioner to pacify the maritime frontier. Now that barbarian bandits were raiding, Jiaozhi alone lacked the strength to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 請發勁卒數萬，會交兵以剪滅之，使交、廣無後患。

translations.literal: They requested dispatch of tens of thousands of elite troops to unite with Jiaozhi forces and extirpate them, so that Jiaozhi and Guang would have no further trouble.
translations.idiomatic: They urged that tens of thousands of crack troops be sent to join Jiaozhi's forces in wiping the bandits out, so that Jiaozhi and Guang would be free of further trouble.

sentences.zh: 上曰：'未可輕舉，慮交州不測朝旨，或致驚駭，不若且委黎桓討擊之，亦當漸至清謐。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'We must not act rashly, for fear that Jiaozhi might not anticipate the court's intent and be alarmed; better to entrust Li Huan for the time being with pursuing and attacking them—in time tranquility will gradually be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "We must not act rashly, lest Jiaozhi fail to grasp the court's intent and be thrown into alarm. Better for now to entrust Li Huan with pursuing and suppressing them; in time the frontier will gradually grow tranquil."

sentences.zh: '今則不復會兵也。」

translations.literal: We shall not assemble troops jointly after all."
translations.idiomatic: We shall not assemble joint forces after all."

sentences.zh: 桓愕然避席，曰：「海賊犯邊，守臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Huan, startled, withdrew from his seat and said: "Sea bandits violating the border is the fault of the frontier minister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, startled, rose from his seat and said, "Sea bandits violating the border are the fault of the frontier minister.

sentences.zh: 聖君容貸，恩過父母，未加誅責。

translations.literal: The sage sovereign has shown forbearance; his grace surpasses that of parents, and no punishment has been imposed.
translations.idiomatic: The sage sovereign has shown forbearance; his grace exceeds that of parents, and no punishment has fallen upon me.

sentences.zh: 自今謹守職約，保永清於漲海。」

translations.literal: From this day forward I shall strictly keep my duties and pledge, and preserve lasting tranquility upon the Zhang Sea."
translations.idiomatic: From this day I shall strictly keep my duties and pledge, and preserve lasting peace upon the Zhang Sea."

sentences.zh: 因北望頓首謝。

translations.literal: He then faced north, prostrated himself, and gave thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He then faced north, kowtowed, and gave thanks.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，進封桓南平王兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Huan was promoted in rank to Prince of Nanping and appointed Chief Minister of the Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Li Huan was promoted to Prince of Nanping and appointed Chief Minister of the Court.

sentences.zh: 桓前遺都知兵馬使阮紹恭、副使趙懷德以金銀七寶裝交椅一、銀盆十、犀角象牙五十枚、絹糸由布萬匹來貢。

translations.literal: Earlier Huan had sent Director of Military Affairs Ruan Shaogong and Vice-envoy Zhao Huaiade to present tribute: one armchair inlaid with gold, silver, and the seven treasures; ten silver basins; fifty rhinoceros horns and elephant tusks; and ten thousand bolts of silk and you cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Huan had sent Ruan Shaogong, Director of Military Affairs, and Vice-envoy Zhao Huaiade to present tribute: one armchair inlaid with gold, silver, and the seven treasures; ten silver basins; fifty rhinoceros horns and elephant tusks; and ten thousand bolts of silk and you cloth.

sentences.zh: 詔陳于萬歲殿太宗神御，許紹恭等拜奠。

translations.literal: An edict ordered these displayed in the Hall of Myriad Years before Emperor Taizong's spirit tablet, and permitted Shaogong and the others to perform obeisance and offerings.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the gifts displayed in the Hall of Myriad Years before Emperor Taizong's spirit tablet, and permitted Shaogong and his party to bow and make offerings.

sentences.zh: 及回，賜桓帶甲馬，詔書慰獎。

translations.literal: When they returned, Huan was bestowed belt, armor, and horses, along with an edict of consolation and commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned, Li Huan was granted a belt, armor, and horses, together with an edict of consolation and commendation.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，又遣行軍司馬黎紹、副使何慶常，以馴犀一、象二、象犬朋二、七寶裝金瓶一來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, he again sent Acting Chief of Staff Li Shao and Vice-envoy He Qingchang to present tribute: one tame rhinoceros, two elephants, two paired young elephants, and one gold vase inlaid with the seven treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping, he again sent Li Shao, Acting Chief of Staff, and Vice-envoy He Qingchang to present tribute: one tame rhinoceros, two elephants, two pairs of young elephants, and one gold vase inlaid with the seven treasures.

sentences.zh: 其年欽州言，交州效誠場民及頭首八州使黃慶集等數百人來投，有詔慰撫，遣還本道。

translations.literal: That year Qin Prefecture reported that several hundred people from Jiaozhi's Xiaocheng field and the tribal head and Eight Prefectures envoy Huang Qingji and others had come to submit; an edict comforted them and ordered them sent back to their circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qin Prefecture reported that several hundred people from Jiaozhi's Xiaocheng field, including the tribal head and Eight Prefectures envoy Huang Qingji, had come to submit. An edict comforted them and ordered them sent back to their circuit.

sentences.zh: 廣南西路言，黎桓迎受官告使黃成雅附奏，自今國朝加恩，願遣使至本道，以寵海裔。

translations.literal: Guangnan West Circuit reported that Li Huan, upon receiving Credential Envoy Huang Chengya, appended a memorial stating that henceforth, as the dynasty extended its grace, he wished an envoy sent to his circuit to honor the maritime frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnan West Circuit reported that when Li Huan received Credential Envoy Huang Chengya, he appended a memorial stating that, as the dynasty now extended its grace, he wished an envoy sent to his circuit to honor the maritime frontier.

sentences.zh: 先是，使至交州，桓即以供奉爲辭，因緣賦斂。

translations.literal: Previously, whenever envoys arrived in Jiaozhi, Huan took their maintenance as a pretext and levied taxes on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, whenever envoys arrived in Jiaozhi, Li Huan took their maintenance costs as a pretext and levied exactions accordingly.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，止令疆吏召授命，不復專使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he ordered that only frontier officials be sent to summon and invest him with authority, and no longer dispatched special envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor learned of this, he ordered that only frontier officials be sent to summon Huan and invest him with his commission, and no longer dispatched special envoys.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，又遣其子攝歡州刺史明提來貢，懇求加恩使至本道慰撫遐裔，許之，仍以明提爲歡州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, he again sent his son Ming Ti, acting prefect of Huan Prefecture, to present tribute, earnestly requesting that a grace-bestowing envoy be sent to his circuit to comfort the distant frontier; this was granted, and Ming Ti was confirmed as prefect of Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde, he again sent his son Ming Ti, acting prefect of Huan Prefecture, to present tribute and earnestly request that an envoy bearing imperial grace be sent to his circuit to comfort the distant frontier. The request was granted, and Ming Ti was confirmed as prefect of Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年上元節，賜明提錢，令與占城、大食使觀燈宴飲，因遣工部員外郎邵曄充國信使。

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival of the second year, Ming Ti was granted money and ordered to view the lanterns and feast with envoys from Champa and Dashi; Shao Ye, Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, was then dispatched as credentialed envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival of the second year, Ming Ti was granted money and invited to view the lanterns and feast with envoys from Champa and Dashi. Shao Ye, Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, was then dispatched as credentialed envoy.

sentences.zh: 三年，桓卒，立中子龍鉞。

translations.literal: In the third year, Huan died; his middle son Long Yue was installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Li Huan died, and his middle son Long Yue was installed as ruler.

sentences.zh: 龍鉞兄龍全劫庫財而遁，其弟龍廷殺龍鉞自立。

translations.literal: Long Yue's elder brother Long Quan plundered the treasury and fled; his younger brother Long Ting killed Long Yue and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Long Yue's elder brother Long Quan plundered the treasury and fled. His younger brother Long Ting killed Long Yue and seized power for himself.

sentences.zh: 龍廷兄明護率扶闌砦兵攻戰。

translations.literal: Long Ting's elder brother Ming Hu led Fulan Stockade troops to attack and fight.
translations.idiomatic: Long Ting's elder brother Ming Hu led troops from Fulan Stockade to attack him.

sentences.zh: 明提以國亂不能還，特詔廣州優加資給。

translations.literal: Ming Ti, unable to return because of the civil turmoil, received a special edict ordering Guangzhou to provide him with extra generous support.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Ti, unable to return because of the civil turmoil at home, received a special edict ordering Guangzhou to provide him with extra generous support.

sentences.zh: 知廣州淩策等言：「桓諸子爭立，衆心離叛，頭首黃慶集、黃秀蠻等千餘人以不從驅率，戮及親族，來投廉州，請發本道二千人平之，慶集等願爲前鋒。」

translations.literal: Prefect of Guangzhou Ling Ce and others reported: "Huan's sons are contending for rule; the people's hearts are divided in rebellion. The tribal heads Huang Qingji, Huang Xiuman, and more than a thousand others, for refusing to follow forced levies and suffering slaughter reaching their kin, have come to submit at Lian Prefecture. They request that two thousand troops of this circuit be dispatched to suppress the disorder, and Qingji and the others wish to serve as vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: Ling Ce, Prefect of Guangzhou, and others reported, "Li Huan's sons are fighting for the throne and the people's hearts are divided. The tribal heads Huang Qingji and Huang Xiuman, together with more than a thousand followers who refused forced levies and saw their kin slaughtered, have fled to Lian Prefecture to submit. They ask that two thousand troops of this circuit be sent to suppress the disorder, and Qingji and his men offer to serve as vanguard."

sentences.zh: 上以桓素忠順，屢修職貢，今幸亂而伐喪，不可。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that since Huan had always been loyal and submissive, repeatedly fulfilling tribute obligations, to take advantage of their chaos and attack them in mourning was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held that since Li Huan had always been loyal and submissive and had repeatedly fulfilled tribute obligations, to exploit their chaos and attack them in their hour of mourning was impermissible.

sentences.zh: 就改國信使邵曄爲緣海安撫使，令曉譬之。

translations.literal: Shao Ye was thereupon changed from credentialed envoy to Pacification Commissioner of the Coastal Circuit and ordered to instruct them by exhortation.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Ye was thereupon reassigned from credentialed envoy to Pacification Commissioner of the Coastal Circuit and ordered to instruct them by persuasion.

sentences.zh: 慶集等仍計口賜田糧。

translations.literal: Qingji and the others were still granted fields and grain rations according to head count.
translations.idiomatic: Qingji and his followers were still granted fields and grain rations according to head count.

sentences.zh: 曄乃貽書交州，諭以朝廷威德，如其自相魚肉，久無定位，偏師問罪，則黎氏盡滅矣。

translations.literal: Shao Ye then sent a letter to Jiaozhi, explaining the court's authority and virtue: if they devoured one another and long remained without a settled ruler, a punitive force would be sent and the Li clan would be utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Ye then sent a letter to Jiaozhi, explaining the court's authority and virtue: if they tore one another apart and long remained without a settled ruler, a punitive force would be sent and the Li clan would be utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 明護懼，即奉龍廷主軍事。

translations.literal: Ming Hu, in fear, thereupon acknowledged Long Ting as master of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Hu, in fear, thereupon acknowledged Long Ting as master of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 龍廷自稱節度、開明王，遂欲修貢。

translations.literal: Long Ting styled himself Military Commissioner and King of Kaiming, and then wished to resume tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Long Ting styled himself Military Commissioner and King of Kaiming, and then sought to resume tribute relations.

sentences.zh: 曄以聞，上曰：「遐荒異俗，不曉事體，何足怪也？」

translations.literal: Shao Ye reported this; the Emperor said: "Remote lands of alien customs do not understand proper decorum—what is there to find strange in that?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao Ye reported this. The Emperor said, "Remote lands of alien custom do not understand proper decorum—what is there to find strange in that?"

sentences.zh: 令削去偽官。

translations.literal: He ordered the false titles removed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the false titles stripped away.

sentences.zh: 曄又言，頭首黃慶集先避亂歸化，其種族尚多，若復遣還，慮遭屠戮。

translations.literal: Shao Ye also reported that the tribal head Huang Qingji had first come over to submit to avoid turmoil, and his clan still numbered many; if sent back, he feared they would suffer massacre.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Ye also reported that the tribal head Huang Qingji had first submitted to escape the turmoil, and his clan still numbered many. If sent back, he feared they would be massacred.

sentences.zh: 詔以慶集隸三班，厘務於郴州，遂許入貢。

translations.literal: An edict placed Qingji in the Third Rank Corps, assigned him duties at Chen Prefecture, and then permitted tribute to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed Qingji in the Third Rank Corps, assigned him duties at Chen Prefecture, and then permitted tribute to proceed.

sentences.zh: 四年，龍廷稱權安南靜海軍留後，遣弟峰州刺史明昶、副使安南掌書記殿中丞黃成雅等來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Long Ting styled himself Acting Military Governor of the Annan Jinghai Army and sent his younger brother Ming Chang, prefect of Feng Prefecture, Vice-envoy Huang Chengya of Annan, Secretariat Drafter and Palace Attendant, and others to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Long Ting styled himself Acting Military Governor of the Annan Jinghai Army and sent his younger brother Ming Chang, prefect of Feng Prefecture, together with Vice-envoy Huang Chengya, Secretariat Drafter and Palace Attendant of Annan, and others to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 會含光殿大宴，上以成雅坐遠，欲稍升位著，訪于宰相王旦，旦曰：「昔子產朝周，周王饗以上卿之禮，子產固辭，受下卿之禮而還。

translations.literal: At a great banquet in the Hall of Incorporating Radiance, because Chengya's seat was distant, the Emperor wished to raise his seating slightly and consulted Chancellor Wang Dan; Dan said: "In ancient times Zichan visited Zhou; the King of Zhou entertained him with the rites due a senior minister, but Zichan firmly declined and accepted the rites of a junior minister before returning.
translations.idiomatic: At a great banquet in the Hall of Incorporating Radiance, because Chengya's seat was far away, the Emperor wished to raise his place slightly and consulted Chancellor Wang Dan. Dan said, "In ancient times Zichan visited Zhou. The King of Zhou entertained him with the rites due a senior minister, but Zichan firmly declined and accepted the rites of a junior minister before returning.

sentences.zh: 國家惠綏遠方，優待客使，固無嫌也。」

translations.literal: Our state benevolently soothes distant regions and generously treats foreign envoys—there is truly nothing objectionable in this."
translations.idiomatic: Our state benevolently soothes distant regions and generously treats foreign envoys—there is truly nothing objectionable in this."

sentences.zh: 乃升成雅於尚書省五品之次。

translations.literal: Chengya was then raised to a seat corresponding to the fifth rank within the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Chengya was then raised to a seat corresponding to the fifth rank within the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 詔拜龍廷特進、檢校太尉，充靜海軍節度觀察處置等使、安南都護，兼御史大夫、上柱國，仍封交趾郡王，食邑三千戶，食實封一千戶。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Long Ting Special Grandee and Acting Grand Marshal, Military Commissioner of the Jinghai Army with observation and disposal authority, Protector General of Annan, also Censor-in-Chief and Pillar of the State; further enfeoffed him as King of Jiaozhi Commandery with a fief of three thousand households and an actual fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Long Ting Special Grandee and Acting Grand Marshal, Military Commissioner of the Jinghai Army with observation and disposal authority, Protector General of Annan, also Censor-in-Chief and Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed him as King of Jiaozhi Commandery with a fief of three thousand households and an actual fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 賜推誠順化功臣，仍賜名至忠，給以旌節。

translations.literal: He was bestowed the title Honorable Merit for Expelling Sincerity and Transforming Submission, also granted the name Zhi Zhong, and given ceremonial insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Honorable Merit for Expelling Sincerity and Transforming Submission, given the name Zhi Zhong, and presented with ceremonial insignia.

sentences.zh: 又追贈桓中書令、南越王。

translations.literal: Li Huan was also posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Counselor and King of Nanyue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was also posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Counselor and King of Nanyue.

sentences.zh: 進奉使黎明昶等並進秩。

translations.literal: The tribute envoys Ming Chang and others all received promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute envoys Ming Chang and the others all received advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，天書降，加翊戴功臣，食邑七百戶，實封三百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, when the Heavenly Writ descended, he was added Honorable Merit for Supporting the Imperial Regime; his fief was increased by seven hundred households and his actual fief by three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, when the Heavenly Writ descended, he was granted Honorable Merit for Supporting the Imperial Regime; his fief was increased by seven hundred households and his actual fief by three hundred.

sentences.zh: 東封畢，加至忠同平章事，食邑一千戶，食實封四百戶。

translations.literal: After the eastern feng rites were complete, Zhi Zhong was made Acting Grand Councillor; his fief was one thousand households and his actual fief four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern feng rites were completed, Zhi Zhong was made Acting Grand Councillor; his fief was increased to one thousand households and his actual fief to four hundred.

sentences.zh: 二年，廣南西路言，欽州蠻人劫海口蜑戶，如洪砦主李文著以輕兵襲逐，中流矢死。

translations.literal: In the second year, Guangnan West Circuit reported that Qin Prefecture tribesmen raided Tanka households at the sea mouth; Ruhong Stockade commander Li Wenzhe pursued them with light troops and died from an arrow wound midstream.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Guangnan West Circuit reported that Qin Prefecture tribesmen had raided Tanka households at the sea mouth. Li Wenzhe, commander of Ruhong Stockade, pursued them with light troops and was killed by an arrow midstream.

sentences.zh: 詔督安南捕賊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Annan to pursue and capture the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Annan to pursue and capture the bandits.

sentences.zh: 明年，執狄獠十三人以獻。

translations.literal: The next year, thirteen Di and Liao captives were seized and presented.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, thirteen Di and Liao captives were seized and presented.

sentences.zh: 至忠又遣推官阮守疆以犀角、象齒、金銀、紋縭等來貢。

translations.literal: Zhi Zhong also sent Administrative Aide Ruan Shoujiang with rhinoceros horn, ivory, gold, silver, patterned silk, and the like as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Zhong also sent Administrative Aide Ruan Shoujiang to present rhinoceros horn, ivory, gold, silver, patterned silk, and the like as tribute.

sentences.zh: 並獻馴犀一。

translations.literal: He also presented one tame rhinoceros.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented one tame rhinoceros.

sentences.zh: 上以犀違土性，不可豢畜，卻不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that the rhinoceros was unsuited to the northern climate and could not be kept in captivity, and declined to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held that the rhinoceros was unsuited to the northern climate and could not be kept in captivity, and declined to accept it.

sentences.zh: 又以逆至忠意，使者既去，乃令縱之海ㄛ。

translations.literal: To avoid countering Zhi Zhong's wishes, after the envoys had departed he ordered it released to the seaside.
translations.idiomatic: Not wishing to thwart Zhi Zhong's intent, after the envoys had departed he ordered the rhinoceros released by the sea.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣使來朝，表求甲胄具裝，詔從其請。

translations.literal: In the third year, envoys came to court; they memorialized requesting armor and full equipment; the edict granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, envoys came to court and memorialized requesting armor and full equipment. An edict granted their request.

sentences.zh: 又求互市於邕州，本道轉運使以聞，上曰：「瀕海之民，數患交州侵寇，仍前止許廉州及如洪砦互市，蓋爲邊隅控扼之所。

translations.literal: They also requested market trade at Yong Prefecture; the circuit transport commissioner reported this; the Emperor said: "Coastal peoples have repeatedly suffered raids from Jiaozhi; as before, market trade is permitted only at Lian Prefecture and Ruhong Stockade—precisely because these are frontier control points.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested market trade at Yong Prefecture. The circuit transport commissioner reported this. The Emperor said, "Coastal peoples have repeatedly suffered raids from Jiaozhi. As before, market trade is permitted only at Lian Prefecture and Ruhong Stockade, precisely because these are frontier control points.

sentences.zh: 今或直趨內地，事頗非便。」

translations.literal: Now to go straight into the interior would be quite inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: To trade directly in the interior would be quite inconvenient."

sentences.zh: 詔令本道以舊制諭之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the circuit to explain the old regulations to them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the circuit to explain the old regulations to them.

sentences.zh: 至忠才年二十六，苛虐不法，國人不附。

translations.literal: Zhi Zhong was only twenty-six years old, harsh and lawless; the people of the state did not support him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Zhong was only twenty-six years old, harsh and lawless, and the people of the realm would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 大校李公蘊尤爲至忠親任，嘗令以黎爲姓。

translations.literal: Senior commander Li Gongyun was especially trusted by Zhi Zhong; he was once ordered to take the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Senior commander Li Gongyun was especially trusted by Zhi Zhong; Zhi Zhong had once ordered him to take the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 其年，遂圖至忠，逐之，殺明提、明昶等，自稱留後，遣使貢奉。

translations.literal: That year, Gongyun then plotted against Zhi Zhong, drove him out, killed Ming Ti, Ming Chang, and others, styled himself Acting Military Governor, and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gongyun plotted against Zhi Zhong, drove him out, killed Ming Ti and Ming Chang among others, styled himself Acting Military Governor, and sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「黎桓不義而得，公蘊尤而效之，甚可惡也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Li Huan obtained power through injustice, and Gongyun has followed his example in surpassing degree—this is deeply repugnant."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Li Huan seized power unjustly, and Gongyun has gone beyond even that—most detestable."

sentences.zh: 然以其蠻俗不足責，遂用桓故事，制授特進、檢校太傅，充靜海軍節度觀察處置等使、安南都護，兼御史大夫、上柱國，封交趾郡王，食邑三千戶，實封一千戶，賜推誠順化功臣。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, considering their barbarian customs not worth reproaching, he followed Huan's precedent and by imperial commission appointed him Special Grandee and Acting Grand Mentor, Military Commissioner of the Jinghai Army with observation and disposal authority, Protector General of Annan, also Censor-in-Chief and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as King of Jiaozhi with a fief of three thousand households and an actual fief of one thousand, and bestowed Honorable Merit for Expelling Sincerity and Transforming Submission.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, considering their barbarian customs not worth reproaching, the court followed Li Huan's precedent and by imperial commission appointed Gongyun Special Grandee and Acting Grand Mentor, Military Commissioner of the Jinghai Army with observation and disposal authority, Protector General of Annan, also Censor-in-Chief and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed him as King of Jiaozhi with a fief of three thousand households and an actual fief of one thousand, and bestowed Honorable Merit for Expelling Sincerity and Transforming Submission.

sentences.zh: 公蘊又表求太宗御書，詔賜百軸。

translations.literal: Gongyun also memorialized requesting Emperor Taizong's imperial writings; an edict granted one hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyun also memorialized requesting Emperor Taizong's imperial writings. An edict granted one hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 四年，祀汾陰後土，公蘊遣節度判官梁任文、觀察巡官黎再嚴以方物來貢，禮成，加公蘊同平章事，食邑一千戶，實封四百戶，任文等並翁優進秩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, after sacrificing to Earth at Fenyin, Gongyun sent Military Commission Aide Liang Renwen and Inspection Circuit Officer Li Zaiyan with local products as tribute; when the rites were complete, Gongyun was made Acting Grand Councillor with a fief of one thousand households and an actual fief of four hundred; Renwen and the others all received honored advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after the sacrifice to Earth at Fenyin, Gongyun sent Military Commission Aide Liang Renwen and Inspection Circuit Officer Li Zaiyan with local products as tribute. When the rites were complete, Gongyun was made Acting Grand Councillor with a fief of one thousand households and an actual fief of four hundred; Renwen and the others all received honored advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，以進奉使李仁美爲誠州刺史、陶慶文爲太常丞，其從隸有道病死者，所賜附還其家。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, summer, Tribute Envoy Li Renmei was made prefect of Cheng Prefecture and Tao Qingwen made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; for attendant retainers who died en route of illness, their granted gifts were sent back to their families.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, summer, Tribute Envoy Li Renmei was made prefect of Cheng Prefecture and Tao Qingwen Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. For attendant retainers who died of illness on the road, the gifts they had received were sent back to their families.

sentences.zh: 是冬，聖祖降，加公蘊開府儀同三司，食邑七百戶，實封三百戶，賜翊戴功臣。

translations.literal: That winter, when the Holy Ancestor descended, Gongyun was made Grand General with Merit equal to the Three Excellencies; his fief was increased by seven hundred households and his actual fief by three hundred; he was bestowed Honorable Merit for Supporting the Imperial Regime.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Holy Ancestor descended, Gongyun was made Grand General with Merit equal to the Three Excellencies; his fief was increased by seven hundred households and his actual fief by three hundred, and he was granted Honorable Merit for Supporting the Imperial Regime.

sentences.zh: 七年春，又加保節守正功臣，食邑一千戶，實封四百戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, spring, he was again added Honorable Merit for Upholding Integrity and Preserving Righteousness; his fief was one thousand households and his actual fief four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, spring, he was again granted Honorable Merit for Upholding Integrity and Preserving Righteousness; his fief was increased to one thousand households and his actual fief to four hundred.

sentences.zh: 詔交趾諸國使入貢者，所在館餼供億，務令豐備。

translations.literal: An edict stated that envoys from Jiaozhi and other states presenting tribute should receive lodging and provisions wherever they passed, with all efforts made to ensure abundance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated that envoys from Jiaozhi and other states presenting tribute should receive lodging and provisions wherever they passed, with every effort made to ensure abundance.

sentences.zh: 其年，遣知唐州刺史陶碩等來貢。

translations.literal: That year, Tao Shuo, acting prefect of Tang Prefecture, and others were sent to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Tao Shuo, acting prefect of Tang Prefecture, and others were sent to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔以碩爲順州刺史，充安南靜海軍行軍司馬；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shuo prefect of Shun Prefecture and Acting Chief of Staff of the Annan Jinghai Army;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Shuo prefect of Shun Prefecture and Acting Chief of Staff of the Annan Jinghai Army;

sentences.zh: 副使吳懷嗣爲澄州刺史，充節度副使。

translations.literal: Vice-envoy Wu Huaisi was made prefect of Cheng Prefecture and Acting Vice Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-envoy Wu Huaisi was made prefect of Cheng Prefecture and Acting Vice Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，交州狄獠張婆看避罪來奔，知欽州穆重穎召之，至中路復拒焉，都巡檢臧嗣遂令如洪砦犒以牛酒。
